I grepped the formal-frontier root for uses of the target declarations and found none outside docs, so the downstream impact is inferred from the in-file proofs. findings.problem: Two Algebra instances are defined from the named ring hom `standardChartHomogeneousLocalizationMap`. The file has no simp or rfl lemma saying `algebraMap (StandardChart R ι i) (StandardChartHomogeneousLocalization R ι i F) x = standardChartHomogeneousLocalizationMap R ι i F x`. It also has none for `algebraMap R (StandardChartHomogeneousLocalization R ι i F) r = map (algebraMap R (StandardChart R ι i) r)`. As a result `algebraMap` and the named map are not unified by simp, and the proofs must restate goals by hand with `change`. The final theorem is stated with the map on its RHS (line 183) but is proved by `change` to an `algebraMap` goal (lines 188–198). The `commutes'` proofs do the same in the other direction.
findings.proposed_change: Add, right after the instances, `@[simp] theorem algebraMap_standardChart_apply (x : StandardChart R ι i) : algebraMap (StandardChart R ι i) (StandardChartHomogeneousLocalization R ι i F) x = standardChartHomogeneousLocalizationMap R ι i F x := rfl`. Add the analogous `@[simp]` lemma for the base-ring algebra, sending `algebraMap R _ r` to `map (algebraMap R (StandardChart R ι i) r)`. Orient both toward the named map. That is the form the theorem statements already use, and it is the form the instance definitions unfold to. Then the `change` blocks in `commutes'` and in `standardChartPolynomialLocalizationEquiv_algebraMap` can be replaced by `simp`/`rw` with these lemmas.
findings.benefit: Users and later files get one canonical normal form for images in the common homogeneous localization. Simp can rewrite `algebraMap` to the named restriction map without definitional unfolding. The proofs shrink to short rewrites.

findings.problem: This is the characteristic computation rule for `standardChartPolynomialLocalizationEquiv`: the equivalence applied to `algebraMap Q _ f` gives the restricted chart image. It is not tagged `@[simp]`. The equivalence is defined with an opaque `__ := ringEquivOfRingEquiv ...` structure, so simp cannot compute it by unfolding. Callers therefore have to apply this lemma by hand, and the file itself uses the unfolding `change` workaround (lines 184–197). The LHS is an application of the new equivalence to a localization-map image, and the RHS is built from the named restriction map and `standardChartEquiv`. Rewriting left to right terminates, and it matches the style of the `@[simp]` computation lemmas such as `standardChartEquiv_X` and `standardChartEquiv_dehomogenizedPolynomial` in StandardChart.lean.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the theorem `@[simp]`. Add the finding-1 lemma `algebraMap ... = standardChartHomogeneousLocalizationMap ...` so that the RHS is already in simp-normal form. Optionally add a `@[simp]` lemma for `(standardChartPolynomialLocalizationEquiv R ι i F).symm` on the images of the chart, or state why it is omitted.
findings.benefit: `simp` can evaluate the equivalence on every element coming from the chart. Downstream users do not have to know the private unfolding. The rule is not a loop, because the equivalence disappears from the RHS.
